questions.stem: In a queue of 60 candidates, a candidate is 10th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 47. New front rank = 10+4 = 14. Back rank = 60 − 14 + 1 = 47.

questions.stem: In a queue of 47 candidates, a candidate is 19th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 26. New front rank = 19+3 = 22. Back rank = 47 − 22 + 1 = 26.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
credit access rural = re ka lu
credit secure banking = re mi su
access secure digital = ze mi ka
rural banking digital = ze su lu
credit access digital = re ze ka
What is the code for “access”?
questions.explanation: Answer: ka. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: credit = re, access = ka, rural = lu, secure = mi, banking = su, digital = ze.

questions.stem:
Statements: X > R = T > U < S.
Conclusions: I. R ≤ T   II. T > S.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is definitely true; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
Statements: W > T < R < P > Q.
Conclusions: I. W > Q   II. P > W.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Either I or II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. Together the alternatives cover every permissible ordering, so either I or II follows.

questions.stem: D is the mother of B. C is the son of B. A is the father of B. How is C related to A?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. A is a parent of B, and C is B’s son. Hence C is A’s grandchild.

questions.stem: A is the brother of E. E is the mother of F. B is the father of A and E. How is A related to F?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. A is the brother of F’s mother E. Therefore A is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: F is the only daughter of D. D is the father of F. H is the son of F. E is the sister of D. How is D related to H?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. D is the father of F, and F is H’s mother. Thus D is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 103 km south, turns left and walks 165 km, then turns left and walks 15 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 187. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 88 km along the initial direction and 165 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(88² + 165²) = 187 km.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some cheques are notes. All notes are loans. No loans is a accounts.
Conclusions:
I. Some cheques are loans.
II. Some notes are accounts.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few cheques are notes. All notes are loans. No loans is a accounts.
Conclusions:
I. Some cheques are not notes.
II. No notes is a accounts.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:
Statements: No cheques is a notes. Some notes are loans. All loans are accounts.
Conclusions:
I. All cheques are accounts.
II. Some accounts are notes.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few cheques are notes. Some notes are loans. All loans are accounts.
Conclusions:
I. All cheques are accounts.
II. No notes is a accounts.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.
